before: Hit-and-run accidents are a real risk on North Charleston's busy roads. When drivers flee the scene, it's often because they are unlicensed, uninsured, impaired, or have outstanding warrants.
after: Hit-and-run accidents are a real risk on North Charleston's busy roads. When drivers flee, it is often because stopping carries its own consequence: two in five who fled fatal crashes and were later identified had no valid license (AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety, 2026); others are uninsured, impaired or wanted on a warrant.

Your own UM coverage is your primary safety net. In South Carolina, UM coverage applies to hit-and-run crashes where the at-fault driver cannot be identified. Key points:

  • SC law requires UM coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150)
  • UM coverage pays for medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering — just like a claim against the at-fault driver's insurance
  • You must report the hit-and-run to police within a reasonable time
  • Your own insurer becomes the opposing party — they will try to minimize your claim just as an at-fault driver's insurer would

Your own UM coverage is your primary safety net. In South Carolina, UM coverage applies to hit-and-run crashes where the at-fault driver cannot be identified, if the conditions of S.C. Code § 38-77-170 are met. Key points:

  • SC law requires UM coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150)
  • UM coverage pays for medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering — just like a claim against the at-fault driver's insurance
  • You must report the hit-and-run to police within a reasonable time; show physical contact, a witness affidavit from someone other than you or, since 2024, a recording of the crash; and not be negligent in failing to identify the driver
  • Your own insurer becomes the opposing party — they will try to minimize your claim just as an at-fault driver's insurer would

before: South Carolina's Crime Victims' Compensation Fund may provide supplemental benefits for hit-and-run victims, including medical expenses and lost wages not covered by insurance.
after: South Carolina's Crime Victims' Compensation Fund may provide supplemental benefits for hit-and-run victims, including medical expenses and lost wages not covered by insurance, if the crash was reported to police within 48 hours and you apply within 180 days, or up to four years for good cause (S.C. Code §§ 16-3-1170, 16-3-1230).
